registers.description: This register is used to trigger software-controlled LPU mode changes. Software can configure LPU_MCTL[TARGET_MODE] to DRUN, LPU_STOP, or LPU_STANDBY only when the current mode is LPU_RUN. Byte and half-word write accesses are not allowed to this register because a predefined key is required to change its value.

bitfields.name: TARGET_MODE
bitfields.description: Target Chip Mode This field provides the target mode to be entered by software. The mechanism to enter into any mode by software requires two write operations: 1. Write key. 2. Write inverted key. NOTE: LPU_SLEEP is entered by configuration of LPU_RUN_CF[LPU_SLEEP].

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: KEY
bitfields.description: This field provides the key to change the target mode. Any write access to the register with a value different from the keys is always ignored. Read access will always return the inverted key KEY: 0101_1010_1111_0000 (0x5AF0) INVERTED KEY: 1010_0101_0000_1111 (0xA50F)

registers.description: The Interrupt Status Register contains flag bits that record an event on the external IRQ pins. When an event as defined in IRQ Rising-Edge Event Enable Register (SIUL2_IREER0) and IRQ Falling-Edge Event Enable Register (SIUL2_IFEER0) occurs, the corresponding flag bit is set. The IRQ Flag bit is set regardless of the state of the corresponding Interrupt Request Enable bit in Interrupt Request Enable Register (SIUL2_IRER0) - Standard. The IRQ Flag bit remains set until cleared by software. The IRQ Flag bits are cleared by writing a '1' to the bits. A write of '0' has no effect. The number of bits implemented is specified by the parameter that defines the number external IRQ pins. This register holds the interrupt flags and supports 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit accesses.

bitfields.description: External Interrupt Status Flag x This flag can be cleared only by writing 1. Writing 0 has no effect. If enabled (SIUL2_IRER[x]), EIF[x] causes an interrupt request.

sub_bitfields.description: No interrupt event has occurred on the pad
An interrupt event as defined by SIUL2_IREER[x] and SIUL2_IFEER[x] has occurred

registers.description: These registers are used to set or clear the respective pads of the device. Parallel port registers for input (PGPDI) and output (PGPDO) are provided to allow a complete port to be written or read in one operation, dependent on the individual pad configuration. The difference between PGPDO and GPDO is that PGPDO registers can be used to set the values of all output pins assigned to a device port with a single 16-bit register write vs. the GPDO registers, which are used to set the value on a specific pin with a byte write. The SIUL2_PGPDO registers access the same physical resource as the SIUL2_PDO and SIUL2_MPGPDO address locations. Some examples of the mapping: • PPDO[0][0] = PDO[0] • PPDO[2][0] = PDO[32] • PPDO[31][15] = PDO[511]

bitfields.name: PPDO
bitfields.description: Parallel Pad Data Out Write or read the data register that stores the value to be driven on the pad in output mode. Access to this register location are coherent with access to the bit-wise GPIO Pad Data Output Registers (SIUL2_GPDO).The x and bit index define which PPDO register bit is equivalent to which PDO register bit according to the following equation: PPDO[x][y] = PDO[(x*16)+y]

registers.description: These registers hold the synchronized input value from the pads. Parallel port registers for input (PGPDI) and output (PGPDO) are provided to allow a complete port to be written or read in one operation, dependent on the individual pad configuration.The difference between PGPDI and GPDI registers is that PGPDI registers can be used to read the values of all input pins assigned to a device port with a single 16-bit register read vs. the GPDI registers, which are used to read the value on a specific pin with a byte read.

bitfields.name: PPDI
bitfields.description: Parallel Pad Data In Reads the current pad value. Access to this register location are coherent with access to the bit-wise GPIO Pad Data Input Registers (SIUL2_GPDI). The x and bit index define which PPDI register bit is equivalent to which PDI register bit according to the following equation: PPDI[x][y] = PDI[(x*16)+y]

registers.description: This register can be used to selectively modify the pad values associated to PPDO[x] [0:15]. The MPGPDO[x] register may only be accessed with 32-bit writes. 8-bit or 16-bit writes will not modify any bits in the register and cause a transfer error response by the module. Read access will return 0.

bitfields.name: MASK
bitfields.description: Mask Field Each bit corresponds to one data bit in the MPPDO[x] register at the same bit location. 0b The associated bit value in the MPPDO[x] field is ignored 1b The associated bit value in the MPPDO[x] field is written

bitfields.name: MPPDO
bitfields.description: Masked Parallel Pad Data Out Write the data register that stores the value to be driven on the pad in output mode. Access to this register location are coherent with access to the bit-wise GPIO Pad Data Output Registers (PDO).The x and bit index define which MPPDO register bit is equivalent to which PDO register bit according to the following equation: MPPDO[x][y] = PDO[(x*16)+y] Functional description

registers.description: The priority registers (PRSn) set the priority of each master port on a per slave port basis and reside in each slave port. The priority register can be accessed only with 32-bit accesses. After the CRSn[RO] bit is set, the PRSn register can only be read; attempts to write to it have no effect on PRSn and result in a bus-error response to the master initiating the write. Two available masters must not be programmed with the same priority level. Attempts to program two or more masters with the same priority level result in a bus-error response and the PRSn is not updated.

bitfields.name: PCTL
bitfields.description: Parking Control Determines the slave port’s parking control. The low-power park feature results in an overall power savings if the slave port is not saturated; however, this forces an extra latency clock when any master tries to access the slave port while not in use because it is not parked on any master.

sub_bitfields.description: When no master makes a request, the arbiter parks the slave port on the master port defined by the PARK bit field
When no master makes a request, the arbiter parks the slave port on the last master to be in control of the slave port
Low-power park. When no master makes a request, the slave port is not parked on a master and the arbiter drives all outputs to a constant safe state

bitfields.name: PARK
bitfields.description: Park Determines which master port the current slave port parks on when no masters are actively making requests and the PCTL bits are cleared. NOTE: Select only master ports that are present on the chip. Otherwise, undefined behavior might occur.

bitfields.name: AULB

sub_bitfields.description: No arbitration is allowed during an undefined length burst

registers.description: Each of the on-platform peripherals has a 4-bit PACRn field, which defines the access levels supported by the given module. Eight PACR fields are grouped together to form a 32-bit PACRx register. The peripheral assignment for each PACR field is defined by the memory map slot that the peripheral is assigned to. See the device's memory map details for the assignments for a particular device. If a peripheral is absent, the corresponding PACR field is not implemented. Reads or writes to the location of an unimplemented PACR register (because all eight of its peripherals are absent) should be avoided to prevent undesired behavior. The following table shows the top-level structure of PACRs. bitfields.description: Supervisor Protect Determines whether the peripheral requires supervisor privilege level for accesses. registers.description: CESR0 provides error status plus configuration information. A global SMPU enable/ disable bit is also included in this register.

bitfields.name: MERR
bitfields.description: Master n error, where the bus master number matches the bit number Indicates a captured error in EARn and EDRn. A bit is set when the hardware detects an error and records the faulting address and attributes. It is cleared by writing one to it. If another error is captured at the exact same cycle as the write, the flag remains set. A find-first-one instruction (or equivalent) can detect the presence of a captured error.

registers.description: CESR1 provides additional error status plus configuration information.

bitfields.name: MEOVR
bitfields.description: Master n error overrun, where the bus master number matches the bit number Each bit in this field signals that another SMPU error for bus master n has occurred before the previous error was processed. The details of the first error are recorded in the EARn and EDRn registers and no information on subsequent errors is recorded until the associated CESR0[MERR] flag is cleared.

registers.description: When the SMPU detects an access error on bus master n, the 32-bit reference address is captured in this read-only register and the corresponding bit in CESR0[MERR] set. Additional information about the faulting access is captured in the corresponding EDRn at the same time.

bitfields.name: EADDR
bitfields.description: Error address Indicates the reference address from bus master n that generated the access error.

registers.description: When the SMPU detects an access error associated with bus master n, 32 bits of error detail are captured in this read-only register and the corresponding bit in CESR0[MERR] isset. Information on the faulting address is captured in the corresponding EARn register at the same time.

bitfields.name: PID[7:0]
bitfields.description: PID of offending access.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: EATTR
bitfields.description: Error attributes Indicates attribute information about the faulting reference.

bitfields.name: ERW
bitfields.description: Error read/write Indicates the access type of the faulting reference.

bitfields.name: EMN
bitfields.description: Error master number Indicates the logical bus master number of the faulting reference. This field is used to determine the bus master that generated the access error.

registers.description: When the SMPU detects an access error associated with bus master n, 32 bits of error detail are captured in this read-only register and the corresponding bit in CESR0[MERR] is set. Information on the faulting address is captured in the corresponding EARn register at the same time.

bitfields.name: EACD
bitfields.description: Error access control detail Indicates the region descriptor with the access error, where the region descriptor number matches the bit number. If EDRn contains a captured error and EACD is all zeroes, an access did not hit in any region descriptor. If only a single EACD bit is set, the access error was caused by a single non-overlapping region descriptor. If two or more EACD bits are set, the access error was caused by an overlapping set of region descriptors. NOTE: When the address hits in a region but there is a PID miss (the PID is reflected in the Error Attribute Detail register), the field EACD = 0, if there is no other error. If there is another error, the EACD will reflect the region of the error (i.e., when it is hit in two regions)

registers.description: Each semaphore gate is implemented in a 4-bit finite state machine, right-justified in a byte data structure. The hardware uses the logical bus master number in conjunction with the data patterns to validate all attempted write operations. Only processor bus masters can modify the gate registers. Once locked, a gate can (and must) be opened (unlocked) by the locking processor core. Multiple gate values can be read in a single access, but only a single gate can be updated via a write operation at a time. Attempted writes with a data value that is neither the unlock value (0x00) nor the appropriate lock value (processor_number + 1) are simply treated as "no operation" and do not affect any gate state. Attempts to write multiple gates in a single aligned access with a size larger than an 8-bit (byte) reference generate an error termination and do not allow any gate state changes.

bitfields.name: RSTGDP
bitfields.description: Reset Gate Data Pattern. This write-only field is accessed with the specified data patterns on the two consecutive writes to enable the gate reset mechanism. For the first write, RSTGDP = E2h while the second write requires RSTGDP = 1Dh.

bitfields.name: RSTGTN
bitfields.description: Reset Gate Number. This 8-bit field specifies the specific hardware gate to be reset. This field is updated by the second write. If RSTGTN < 64, then reset the single gate defined by RSTGTN, else reset all the gates.

registers.description: This section describes how the Reset Gate register fields appear when the register is read. See Reset Gate Write (SEMA42_RSTGT_W) for the description of the register's overall operation and how the register fields appear when the register is written.

bitfields.name: ROZ
bitfields.description: This field always returns the value 0 when read.

bitfields.name: RSTGSM
bitfields.description: Reset Gate Finite State Machine. Reads of the SEMA42_RSTGT register return the encoded state machine value. Note the RSTGSM = 10 state is valid for only a single machine cycle, so it is impossible for a read to return this value. The reset state machine is maintained in a 2-bit, 3-state implementation, defined as:

sub_bitfields.description: Idle, waiting for the first data pattern write.
Waiting for the second data pattern write.

The 2-write sequence has completed. Generate the specified gate reset(s). After the reset is performed, this machine returns to the idle (waiting for first data pattern write) state. The "01" state persists for only one clock cycle. Software cannot observe this state.
This state encoding is never used and therefore reserved.

bitfields.name: RSTGMS
bitfields.description: Reset Gate Bus Master. This 4-bit read-only field records the logical number of the bus master performing the gate reset function. The reset function requires that the two consecutive writes to this register must be initiated by the same bus master to succeed. This field is updated each time a write to this register occurs. The association between system bus master port numbers, the associated bus master device, and the logical processor number is SoC-specific. Consult the device reference manual for this information.

bitfields.name: RSTGTN
bitfields.description: Reset Gate Number. This 8-bit field specifies the specific hardware gate to be reset. This field is updated by the second write. If RSTGTN < 64, then reset the single gate defined by RSTGTN, else reset all the gates.

bitfields.name: MPROT

If MPROT is enabled, INTC_MPROT[ID] can write to any valid entry of the INTC memory map but other masters can only write to their assigned resources. Once MPROT is enabled by a master, only that master may modify INTC_MPROT.

registers.description: The INTC_CPRn masks any peripheral or software-settable interrupt request that is set at the same or lower priority as the current value of the INTC_CPRn[PRI] field from generating an interrupt request to the processor. When the INTC Interrupt Acknowledge register (INTC_IACKRn) is read in software vector mode or the interrupt acknowledge signal from the processor is asserted in hardware vector mode, the value of PRI is pushed onto the LIFO, and PRI is updated with the priority of the preempting interrupt request. When the INTC end-of-interrupt register (INTC_EOIRn) is written, the LIFO is popped into the INTC_CPRn PRI field. An exception case in hardware vector mode to this behavior is described in Hardware vector mode. The masking priority can be raised or lowered by writing to the PRI field, supporting the priority ceiling protocol. See Priority ceiling protocol. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=0 (disabled), all processors have write access to this register. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 (enabled), the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] or the corresponding processor has write access, otherwise, a termination error is asserted.

registers.description: The Interrupt Acknowledge Register for Processor n provides a value which can be used to load the address of an ISR from a vector table. The vector table can be composed of addresses of the ISRs specific to their respective interrupt vectors. Also, in software vector mode, the INTC_IACKRn has side effects from reads unless INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 and processor with master ID (0-3) != INTC_MPROT[ID]. Therefore, it must not be read speculatively while in this mode. The side effects are the same regardless of the size of the read. Reading the INTC_IACKRn does not have side effects in hardware vector mode. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=0 (disabled), all processors have read and write access to this register. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 (enabled), the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] or the corresponding processor has read and write access, otherwise, a termination error is asserted.

registers.description: Writing to the INTC_EOIRn signals the end of the servicing of the interrupt request. When the INTC_EOIRn is written, the priority last pushed on the LIFO is popped into INTC_CPRn. The values and size of data written to the INTC_EOIRn are ignored. Those values and sizes written to this register neither update the INTC_EOIRn contents nor affect whether the LIFO pops. Typically, when you write to this register, write four all- zero bytes. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=0 (disabled), all processors have write access to this register. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 (enabled), the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] or the corresponding processor has write access, otherwise, a termination error is asserted.

registers.description: The INTC_SSCIR registers support the setting or clearing of software-settable interrupt requests. These registers contain independent sets of bits to set and clear a corresponding flag bit by software. Unlike the SWT bit in the PSRs, the INTC_SSCIR registers do not require a read-modify-write. With the exception of being set by software, this flag bit behaves the same as a flag bit set within a peripheral. This flag bit generates an interrupt request within the INTC just like a peripheral interrupt request. Writing a 1 to SET will leave SET unchanged at 0 but will set CLR. Writing a 0 to SET will have no effect. CLR is the flag bit. Writing a 1 to CLR will clear it. Writing a 0 to CLR will have no effect. If a 1 is written to a pair of SET and CLR bits at the same time, CLR is asserted, regardless of whether CLR was asserted before the write. See Figure 23-2 for limitations on writing to this register. Any processor will be allowed to write to any of the SET bits in the INTC_SSCIRn registers. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=0 (disabled), all processors can write to the CLR bit. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 (enabled), the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] or the corresponding processor can write to the CLR bit, otherwise, a termination error is asserted.

bitfields.name: Reserved

bitfields.name: SET
bitfields.description: Set flag bits. Writing a 1 will set the corresponding CLR bit. Writing a 0 will have no effect. Each SET is read as a 0.

bitfields.name: CLR
bitfields.description: Clear flag bits. CLR is the flag bit. Writing a 1 to CLR will clear it provided that a 1 is not written simultaneously to its corresponding SET bit. Writing a 0 to CLR will have no effect.

sub_bitfields.description: Interrupt request not pending within INTC.

registers.description: The Priority Select Registers support the selection of an individual priority for each source of interrupt request, and the routing of the request to one or more processors. The unique vector of each peripheral or software-settable interrupt request determines which INTC_PSRn is assigned to that interrupt request. The software-settable interrupt requests are assigned the lowest numbered vectors, and their priorities are configured in the lowest numbered INTC_PSR registers. The peripheral interrupt requests are assigned to vectors immediately following the software-settable interrupt requests, and their priorities are configured in the immediately following INTC_PSR registers. The peripheral interrupt requests are assigned vectors 32-1023, and their priorities are configured in INTC_PSR32-1023, respectively. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=0 (disabled), all processors have write access. If INTC_MPROT[MPROT]=1 (enabled), the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] or the corresponding processor has write access to INTC_PSRn[PRC_SEL,SWT], otherwise, a termination error is asserted. When writing the INTC_PSRn[PRI], only the processor with master ID (0-3) = INTC_MPROT[ID] and the processor whose master ID (0-3) matches the setting of the INTC_PSRn[PRC_SEL] will be allowed to write the INTC_PSRn[PRI]. An attempt by any other processor to write the INTC_PSRn[PRI] will result in a termination error. See Figure 23-2 for limitations on writing to this register.

Writing a '1' to SWTn sets the bit. On the interrupt acknowledge cycle, the SWTn bit is cleared. The SWT function works both in hardware and software vector mode. registers.description: This register provides the status of the halt handshake abort request, if any, from the system. Depending on when the halt abort request was received, the halt handshake may or may not be aborted. If the abort is successful and the dividers were not updated, the value of DIV_UPD_ABRTD is set as 1. In case the DIV_UPD_ABRTD bit is set, the software should clear the status by writing a 1 to bit 0 of this register and should initiate the divider update trigger at some later point. Till such a time that the dividers are updated again, the current division value of the dividers would not match the divider configuration. This register is reset only on PHASE3 reset.

sub_bitfields.description: The abort is successful and the dividers were not updated, the value of DIV_UPD_ABRTD is set to 1.

registers.description: This register selects whether the system clock divider ratios will change from the current configuration to the configuration in the next update. If the value of SYS_DIV_RATIO_CHNG is ‘1’ at the time of a write to the CGM_DIV_UPD_TRIG register and a pre-loaded system clock divider update is pending, the crossbar is halted while the system clock divider update takes place. If the value of SYS_DIV_RATIO_CHNG is ‘0’, the crossbar switch is not halted. This register has no effect if the system clock divider update is configured in the CGM_DIV_UPD_TYPE register to be immediate. An example of a divider ratio not changing is divider 0 changes from divide by 1 to divide by 2, and divider 1 changes from divide by 2 to divide by 4. The ratio is 1:2 in both configurations. An example of a divider ratio changing is divider 0 changes from divide by 1 to divide by 2, and divider 1 changes from divide by 2 to divide by 6. The ratio changes from 1:2 to 1:3. The value of SYS_DIV_RATIO_CHNG is returned to ‘1’ automatically on each write to the CGM_DIV_UPD_TRIG register. Software must never write a ‘0’ to the SYS_DIV_RATIO_CHNG bit if the system clock divider ratios change from the current configuration to the next configuration. This can potentially cause errors in the crossbar which lead to lost data.

registers.description: The Module Configuration register (MCR) provides access to low power, debug, and filter control bits.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: MDIS
bitfields.description: Module Disable The MDIS bit forces the filter to enter a low power state. After this bit is asserted the clock for the module is removed thus filter operation is not possible. The access to filter registers is allowed.

sub_bitfields.description: Input Glitch Filter is not in low power mode due to MDIS bit
Input Glitch Filter is in low power mode

bitfields.name: FRZ
bitfields.description: Freeze bit for debug operation The FRZ bit enables the Input Glitch Filter to enter freeze mode (debug mode) when a system level signal request the module enters freeze (debug) mode. Once in freeze mode the filter operation is disabled meaning that transitions on the input signal will not propagate through the filter output. The bypass FBP bit can be used by the software to force the filter output to be the same as the filter input. In this mode FOH and FOL also can be used to define the filter output state.

bitfields.name: FBP
bitfields.description: Force Bypass This bit is self-negated thus is only read as zero. Writing 1 to this bit while in freeze mode forces the filter to bypass the value in the input to the filter output, thus allowing a software control on the filter. This bit is functional only in freeze mode.

sub_bitfields.description: transfer input signal value to the filter output

bitfields.name: FOH
bitfields.description: Force filter output high If set, this bit forces the Input Glitch Filter output to ‘1’. This bit is functional only in debug mode. It is self- negated thus always read as zero.

bitfields.name: FOL
bitfields.description: Force filter output low If set this bit forces the Input Glitch Filter output to ‘0’. This bit is functional only in debug mode. It is self- negated thus always read as zero.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: IMM
bitfields.description: Immediate edge propagation control bit The IMM bit controls the propagation of an edge through the filter. If asserted, this bit defines that an edge at the filter input propagates through the filter output independent of the prescaler settings. In bypass mode the propagation delay is three system clock cycles. If negated, the signal propagation depends upon the prescaler settings. The filter hardware will only allow chages to this bit if the filter is disabled, FGEN =

sub_bitfields.description: edge propagation within three system clock cycles

bitfields.name: PSSEL
bitfields.description: Prescaler selection bit The PSSEL selects if the prescaler used by the Input Glitch Filter is from internal source (internal prescaler counter) or from external source. The filter hardware will only allow changes to this bit if the filter is disabled, FGEN=0.

bitfields.name: POL
bitfields.description: Output polarity bit This bit sets the polarity of the filter output to inverted or not inverted. The polarity control implemented by the POL bit is applied at the filter output stage thus also changing the reset state of the output, even if the filter is disabled by the FGEN bit. The filter hardware will only allow changes to this bit if the filter is disabled, FGEN=0.

bitfields.name: FGEN
bitfields.description: Filter global enable This control bit enables the filter operation, meaning that if the filter is enabled the filtering selected types are applied to the rising and falling edges of the input signal. If the filter is not enabled, then the filter output remains unchanged independent of the filter input signal. Note that the filter output state is affected by the POL bit when the filter is disabled.

sub_bitfields.description: filter is disabled: filter output keeps current state.
filter is enabled: filtering is applied to selected edges.

bitfields.name: FFM
bitfields.description: Falling edge filter type selection This bit field selects the filter type for the filter input signal falling edge. The filter hardware will only allow changes to this bit if the filter is disabled, FGEN=0.

sub_bitfields.description: bypass: edge is propagated to filter output without any filtering in three system clock cycles
windowing: windowing filter is selected for the falling edge
integrating: integrating filter is selected for the falling edge
integrating-hold: integrating-hold filter is selected for the falling edge
windowing with post sample: windowing filter with post sample is selected for the falling edge

bitfields.name: RFM
bitfields.description: Rising edge filter type selection This bit field selects the filter type for the input signal rising edge. The filter hardware will only allow changes to this bit if the filter is disabled, FGEN=0.

sub_bitfields.description: bypass: edge is propagated to filter output without any filtering in three system clock cycles
windowing: windowing filter is selected for the rising edge
integrating: integrating filter is selected for the rising edge
integrating-hold: integrating-hold filter is selected for the rising edge
windowing with post sample: windowing filter with post sample is selected for the rising edge

registers.description: The Module status register (MSR) provides access to filter status bits and corresponding clear bits as well as access to the state of filter input and output signals.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: WEDGE
bitfields.description: Filter is active waiting for an edge This bit is set when the filter is enabled but the internal counter is not active. It indicates that the filter is waiting for an edge to occur at the filter input. It is set by the Input Glitch Filter hardware and cleared by the software by writing 1 to the bit. Since the intention of this bit is to capture the dynamic of the filter hardware, it should be cleared after the read thus being able to capture a new event.

sub_bitfields.description: Input Glitch Filter is disabled or the internal counter is active
Input Glitch Filter is waiting for an edge

bitfields.name: FEDGE
bitfields.description: Filter is active processing an edge This bit is set during the filter active state thus when the filter internal counter is counting, processing an edge in a filtering mode. It is cleared by the software by writing 1 to the bit. Since the intention of this bit is to capture the dynamic of the filter hardware, it should be cleared after the read thus being able to capture a new event.

sub_bitfields.description: Input Glitch Filter internal counter is not active
Input Glitch Filter internal counter is active

bitfields.name: RNDET
bitfields.description: Rise noise detected bit This bit indicates that the filter filtered out noise in the input signal after a rising edge was detected. The criteria to set this bit is when a rising edge is detected thus starting the filter counter and before this edge pass through the filter (if filter is in integrating filter types) or during a window (if filter is in windowing filter types) another edge occurs in the input signal. This bit is set by a noise detection and cleared by the software by writing 1 to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: noise was detected after a rising edge

bitfields.name: FNDET
bitfields.description: Fall noise detected bit This bit indicates that the filter filtered out noise in the input signal after a falling edge was detected. The criteria to set this bit is when a falling edge is detected, thus starting the filter counter, and, if the filter is in integrating types, before this edge passes through the filter, or, in windowing types, when another edge occurs in the input signal during a window. This bit is set by a noise detection and cleared by the software by writing 1 to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: noise was detected after a falling edge

bitfields.name: FLI
bitfields.description: Filter input The FLI bit follows the state of the filter input value as captured by the filter input logic, which is affected by the IMM bit and prescaler settings.

bitfields.name: FLO
bitfields.description: Filter output The FLO bit follows the state of the filter output value considering the POL bit state.

This bit has no effect on conversion of a channel when presampling on that channel is disabled (for example, PSRx[PRESy] = 0 , where x = register index and y = channel number).

bitfields.name: INPSAMP
bitfields.description: Configuration of sampling phase duration. This value tells the sample period duration in terms of the SAR Controller operating clock. The minimum acceptable value is 8. Setting a lower value automatically takes 8 cycles. NOTE: The Bandgap voltage sampling time is controlled by CTR0[INPSAMP]. CTR0[INPSAMP] is also used for the external channel sample time. When the user software needs to sample the Bandgap voltage, it must change the CTR0[INPSAMP] value to allow for a longer time while the Bandgap is being sampled, then change its value back to the normal value for sampling external channels.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: DSD
bitfields.description: The delay between the external decode signals and the beginning of the sampling phase. It is used to take into account the settling time of the external mux. The decode signal delay is calculated as (DSD x 1/ Frequency of System Clock).

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: PDED
bitfields.description: The delay between the power down bit reset and the start of conversion. The power down delay is calculated as (PDED x 1/[ADC_clock_frequency]).

registers.description: Note It is important to note that the content of the CDATA field is affected by the setting of the ADC_MCR[WLSIDE] field, which controls whether the data is left aligned or right aligned. When ADC_MCR[WLSIDE]=1 (data to be left aligned), the CDATA field is left aligned from bit 16 to bit (16 + resolution - 1). When ADC_MCR[WLSIDE]=0 (data to be right aligned), the CDATA field is right aligned from bit (32-resolution) to bit 31. All other fields are unaffected.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: VALID
bitfields.description: Used to notify when the data is valid (a new value has been written). It is automatically cleared when data is read.

bitfields.name: OVERW
bitfields.description: Overwrite data Used to notify when a conversion data is overwritten by a newer result. The new data is written or discarded according to the OWREN bit of MCR register.

bitfields.name: RESULT
bitfields.description: These two bits reflect the mode of conversion for the corresponding channel.

sub_bitfields.description: Data is a result of Normal conversion mode
Data is a result of Injected conversion mode
Data is a result of BCTU conversion mode

registers.description: This register controls the Offset calculation, Calibration and BIST functionality with Averaging option. The averaging function has no effect in other conversion modes.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. When writing to this register, do not change the default value of this field.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. When writing to this register, do not change the default value of this field. NOTE: The reset value of this field depends on the resolution of the ADC instance. • Reset value is 01b for 12-bit ADC instances • Reset value is 10b for 10-bit ADC instances

bitfields.name: TSAMP
bitfields.description: Test Sample period in Calibration, BIST and Offset calculation process.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. When writing to this register, do not change the default value of this field.

bitfields.name: C_T_BUSY
bitfields.description: This bit indicates that ADC is doing internal operations for BIST or Calibration. This is set when the TEST_EN bit is set.

sub_bitfields.description: ADC is busy in calibration or test operation

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. When writing to this register, do not change the default value of this field.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. The default value must not change. Always write the default value to this field.

bitfields.name: NR_SMPL
bitfields.description: Number of Samples for averaging. NOTE: The sample setting is providing a trade-off between calibration time and accuracy. For best accuracy 512 samples are recommended. The 16 sample setting shall only be used for applications which require very fast calibration time at the expense of accuracy.

bitfields.name: AVG_EN
bitfields.description: Average Enable (for Calibration only).

bitfields.name: TEST_FAIL
bitfields.description: Test Fail. This bit indicates the status of Calibration output. This bit sets automatically if tests are aborted prematurely by any normal conversion or tests complete but one of them fails. This bit is cleared by writing 1 to it or on restarting of test by writing 1 to TEST_EN

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: TEST_EN
bitfields.description: Enable the test.

sub_bitfields.description: Enable the test (self clearing) (once set it cannot be overwritten till it resets)

registers.description: This register contains the user configured offset and Gain values used by ADC for data processing and have all the bits valid (MSB through LSB). OFFSET and Gain Calibration values can be either positive or negative, so they need to be in 2's complement format with MSB as sign bit.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: GAIN_USER
bitfields.description: Gain User (2's complement format)

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: OFFSET_USER
bitfields.description: Offset User (2's complement format)

registers.description: Access: • Supervisor read/write • User read/write

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: DMAEN
bitfields.description: DMA Enable Enables the DMA transfer triggered from the CMP module. When this field is set, a DMA request is asserted when CFR or CFF is set.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: IER
bitfields.description: Comparator Interrupt Enable Rising Enables the CFR interrupt from the CMP. When this field is set, an interrupt will be asserted when CFR is set.

bitfields.name: IEF
bitfields.description: Comparator Interrupt Enable Falling Enables the CFF interrupt from the CMP. When this field is set, an interrupt will be asserted when CFF is set.

bitfields.name: CFR
bitfields.description: Analog Comparator Flag Rising Detects a rising-edge on COUT, when set, during normal operation. CFR is cleared by writing 1 to it. During Stop modes, CFR is level sensitive

sub_bitfields.description: A rising edge has not been detected on COUT.
A rising edge on COUT has occurred.

bitfields.name: CFF
bitfields.description: Analog Comparator Flag Falling Detects a falling-edge on COUT, when set, during normal operation. CFF is cleared by writing 1 to it. During Stop modes, CFF is level senstive .

sub_bitfields.description: A falling edge has not been detected on COUT.
A falling edge on COUT has occurred.

bitfields.name: COUT
bitfields.description: Analog Comparator Output Returns the current value of the Analog Comparator output, when read. The field is reset to 0 and will read as C0[INVT] when the Analog Comparator module is disabled, that is, when C0[EN] = 0. Writes to this field are ignored.

bitfields.name: FPR
bitfields.description: Filter Sample Period Specifies the sampling period, in bus clock cycles, of the comparator output filter, when C1[SE] = 0. Setting FPR to 0x0 disables the filter. Filter programming and latency details are provided in the CMP functional description. This field has no effect when C0[SE ]= 1. In that case, the external SAMPLE signal is used to determine the sampling period.

bitfields.name: SE
bitfields.description: Sample Enable At any given time, either SE or WE can be set. If a write to this register attempts to set both, then SE is set and WE is cleared. However, avoid writing ones to both bit locations because this "11" case is reserved.

bitfields.name: WE
bitfields.description: Windowing Enable At any given time, either SE or WE can be set. If a write to this register attempts to set both, then SE is set and WE is cleared. However, avoid writing ones to both bit locations because this "11" case is reserved.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: PMODE
bitfields.description: Power Mode Select

sub_bitfields.description: Low Speed (LS) comparison mode is selected.
High Speed (HS) comparison mode is selected.

bitfields.name: INVT
bitfields.description: Comparator invert This bit allows selecting the polarity of the analog comparator function. It is also driven to the COUT output (on both the device pin and as C0[COUT]) when CR1[OPE]=0.

sub_bitfields.description: Does not invert the comparator output.

bitfields.name: COS
bitfields.description: Comparator Output Select

sub_bitfields.description: Set CMPO to equal COUT (filtered comparator output).
Set CMPO to equal COUTA (unfiltered comparator output).

bitfields.name: OPE
bitfields.description: Comparator Output Pin Enable The OPE bit enables the path from the comparator output to a selected pin.

sub_bitfields.description: When OPE is 0, the comparator output (after window/filter settings dependent on software configuration) is not available to a packaged pin.
When OPE is 1, and if the software has configured the comparator to own a packaged pin, the comparator is available in a packaged pin.

bitfields.name: EN
bitfields.description: Comparator Module Enable The EN bit enables the Analog Comparator Module. When the module is not enabled, the analog part remains in the off state, and consumes no power. When the same input is selected from analog mux to the positive and negative port, the comparator is disabled automatically.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: FILTER_CNT
bitfields.description: Filter Sample Count This field specifies the number of consecutive samples that must agree prior to the comparator ouput filter accepting a new output state. For information regarding filter programming and latency, please see the Functional Description.

sub_bitfields.description: Filter is disabled. If SE = 1, then COUT is a logic zero (this is not a legal state, and is not recommended). If SE = 0, COUT = COUTA.
1 consecutive sample must agree (comparator output is simply sampled).

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved.

bitfields.name: HYSTCTR
bitfields.description: Comparator hard block hysteresis control

sub_bitfields.description: The hard block output has no hysteresis internally.
The hard block output has 20 mv hysteresis internally.
The hard block output has 40 mv hysteresis internally.
The hard block output has 60 mv hysteresis internally.

bitfields.name: DPSEL
bitfields.description: DAC output to Plus side ANMUX selection

sub_bitfields.description: The analog mux_out (selected from the external inputs) is selected as the comparator plus side input.
The DAC out is selected as the comparator plus side input.

bitfields.name: DMSEL
bitfields.description: DAC output to Minus side ANMUX selection

sub_bitfields.description: The analog mux_out (selected from the external input) is selected as the comparator minus side input.
The DAC out is selected as the comparator input.

bitfields.name: PSEL
bitfields.description: Plus Input MUX Control Determines which input is selected for the plus input of the comparator. NOTE: When an inappropriate operation selects the same input for both MUXes, the comparator automatically shuts down to prevent itself from becoming a noise generator. Note: For the round robin mode of operation, the MSEL and PSEL bitfields in CMPx_C1 register must have different values.

bitfields.name: MSEL
bitfields.description: Minus Input MUX Control Determines which input is selected for the minus input of the comparator. NOTE: When an inappropriate operation selects the same input for both MUXes, the comparator automatically shuts down to prevent itself from becoming a noise generator. Note: For the round robin mode of operation, the MSEL and PSEL bitfields in CMPx_C1 register must have different values.

bitfields.name: DACEN
bitfields.description: DAC Enable This bit is used to enable the DAC. When the DAC is disabled, it is powered down to conserve power.

bitfields.name: VRSEL
bitfields.description: Supply Voltage Reference Source Select

sub_bitfields.description: Vin1 is selected as resistor ladder network supply reference Vin.
Vin2 is selected as resistor ladder network supply reference Vin.

bitfields.name: VOSEL
bitfields.description: DAC Output Voltage Select This bit selects an output voltage from one of 64 distinct levels. DACO = (Vin/64) * (VOSEL[5:0] + 1), so the DACO range is from Vin/64 to Vin.

registers.description: Access: • Supervisor read/write • User read/write

bitfields.name: RRE
bitfields.description: Round-Robin Enable This bit enables the round-robin operation.

bitfields.name: RRIE
bitfields.description: Round-Robin interrupt enable This bit enables the interrupt/wake-up when the comparison result changes for a given channel.

sub_bitfields.description: The round-robin interrupt is enabled when a comparison result changes from the last sample.

bitfields.name: FXMP
bitfields.description: Fixed MUX Port This bit is used to fix the analog mux port for the round-robin mode.

sub_bitfields.description: The Plus port is fixed. Only the inputs to the Minus port are swept in each round.
The Minus port is fixed. Only the inputs to the Plus port are swept in each round.

bitfields.name: FXDACI
bitfields.description: Fix DAC input to the fixed mux port side

sub_bitfields.description: The DAC output is not used as the reference input to the fixed mux port.
The DAC output is used as the reference input to the fixed mux port, regardless of the FXMXCH configuration.

bitfields.name: FXMXCH
bitfields.description: Fixed channel selection This field indicates which channel in the mux port is fixed in a given round-robin mode. If FXDACI is set, FXMXCH has no effect.

sub_bitfields.description: Channel 0 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 1 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 2 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 3 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 4 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 5 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 6 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.
Channel 7 is selected as the fixed reference input for the fixed mux port.

bitfields.name: NSAM

sub_bitfields.description: The comparison result is sampled in .

The sampling takes place 2 round-robin clock cycles after the next cycle of the round-robin clock.

bitfields.name: ACOn

bitfields.name: IEN1
bitfields.description: Interrupt enable bit for ADC1DR new data. This bit enables an interrupt request if the ADC1DR register is written by the hardware, meaning that there is new conversion data available. It also enables an interrupt request to be issued if there is an overrun in the ADC1DR register, meaning that the previous data in this register was overwritten by a new data. See also NDATA1 and DATAOVR1 in the MSR register. If DMA1 bit is set the interrupt for ADC1DR new data is disabled but the interrupt for ADC1DR data overrun remains enabled. In this case if an overrun condition occurs an interrupt request is generated.

bitfields.name: IEN0
bitfields.description: Interrupt enable bit for ADC0DR new data. This bit enables an interrupt request if the ADC0DR register is written by the hardware, meaning that there is new conversion data available. It also enables an interrupt request to be issued if there is an overrun in the ADC0DR register, meaning that the previous data in this register was overwritten by a new data. See also NDATA0 and DATAOVR0 in the MSR register. If DMA0 bit is set the interrupt for ADC0DR new data is disabled but the interrupt for ADC0DR data overrun remains enabled. In this case if an overrun condition occurs an interrupt request is generated.

bitfields.name: LOOP
bitfields.description: LOOP bit The LOOP bit , defined if the current trigger should execute a loop, meaning that the conversion triggered by the input trigger is executed again until the LOOP bit is cleared. Each time the new conversion is triggered it should win the priority evaluation among all pending triggers. It is only executed if it is the highest priority triggered conversion at the moment the conversion starts.

registers.description: Coming out from reset state the protection is enabled. In order to allow writes to protected registers it is necessary to write a special code in a 4-bit field. There are two possible codes that allow writes thus removing the protection. One 4-bit code that permanently disables the protection mechanism and another code that disables the protection during one write cycle to a protected register. After that the state of the protection code returns to its initial (protected) state. Access: User read/write

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved.

bitfields.name: PROTEC_CODE
bitfields.description: The Protection code sets protection for the write protected registers There are two codes which disables the protection for the write protected registers. One code disables the write protection permanently and another code disables the protection for one write access only. NOTE: This field is writable only if the MCR[MDIS] bit is 0.

sub_bitfields.description: This code defines that the protected registers are not in the protected mode, thus writes are enabled.

Protection temporarily deactivated. This code disables the protection for writes on the protected registers for one write cycle operation. After that the protection code is reset to the initial state "0000" thus restoring the protection for the protected registers. Protection is active for other values

registers.description: The Software Trigger register allows the software to trigger any of the conversions associated with the Trigger Configuration registers. In order to avoid ambiguity in the conversion results regarding the source of trigger (if from hardware or from the software) the trigger enable (TRIGEN) bit in the Trigger Configuration register should be cleared when the software trigger is used thus the trigger for that configuration register is only issued by the SFTRGR register. This register is write protected by the WRPROT register. If protection is enabled writes to this register do not modify the register content and generates a transfer error. All bits in this register are set by the software and cleared by the hardware. Access: User read/write; this register is write protected by the BCTU_WRPROT register.

registers.description: This register is used to trigger software-controlled mode changes. Depending on the modes as enabled by ME_ME register bits, configurations corresponding to unavailable modes are reserved and access to ME_<mode>_MC registers must respect this for successful mode requests.

bitfields.name: TARGET_MODE
bitfields.description: Target chip mode These bits provide the target chip mode to be entered by software programming. The mechanism to enter into any mode by software requires the write operation twice: first time with key, and second time with inverted key. These bits are automatically updated by hardware while entering SAFE on hardware request. Also, while exiting from the STOP0 modes on hardware exit events, these are updated with the appropriate RUN0…3 mode value.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: KEY
bitfields.description: Control key — These bits enable write access to this register. Any write access to the register with a value different from the keys is ignored. Read access will always return inverted key. KEY: 0101101011110000 (0x5AF0) INVERTED KEY: 1010010100001111 (0xA50F)

registers.description: This register allows a way to disable the chip modes which are not required for a given chip. RESET_FUNC, SAFE, DRUN, RESET_DEST, and RUN0 modes are always enabled.

bitfields.name: Reserved

registers.description: This register provides the current interrupt status.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: I_ICONF_CC
bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration interrupt (core configuration) — This bit is set if a write access to one of the ME_CADDRn registers is attempted while a mode transition is in progress.

sub_bitfields.description: No write to an ME_CADDRn register was attempted during an ongoing mode transition
A write to an ME_CADDRn register was attempted during an ongoing mode transition

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved and can be set to 1 by hardware during some mode transitions. The setting of this bit has no impact on the device. This field is reserved.

bitfields.name: I_ICONF
bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration interrupt — This bit is set whenever a write operation to ME_<mode>_MC registers with invalid mode configuration is attempted. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: No invalid mode configuration interrupt occurred
Invalid mode configuration interrupt is pending

bitfields.name: I_IMODE
bitfields.description: Invalid mode interrupt — This bit is set whenever an invalid mode transition is requested. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

bitfields.name: I_SAFE
bitfields.description: SAFE mode interrupt — This bit is set whenever the chip enters SAFE mode on hardware requests generated in the system. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

bitfields.name: I_MTC
bitfields.description: Mode transition complete interrupt — This bit is set whenever the mode transition process completes (S_MTRANS transits from 1 to 0). It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit. This mode transition interrupt bit will not be set while entering low-power modes STOP0, or STANDBY0.

sub_bitfields.description: No mode transition complete interrupt occurred
Mode transition complete interrupt is pending

registers.description: This register controls whether an event generates an interrupt or not.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: M_ICONF_CC
bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration (core configuration) interrupt mask

sub_bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration (core configuration) interrupt is masked
Invalid mode configuration (core configuration) interrupt is enabled

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: M_ICONF
bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration interrupt mask

sub_bitfields.description: Invalid mode configuration (core configuration) interrupt is masked
Invalid mode configuration (core configuration) interrupt is enabled

bitfields.name: M_IMODE
bitfields.description: Invalid mode interrupt mask

bitfields.name: M_SAFE
bitfields.description: SAFE mode interrupt mask

bitfields.name: M_MTC
bitfields.description: Mode transition complete interrupt mask

sub_bitfields.description: Mode transition complete interrupt is masked
Mode transition complete interrupt is enabled

registers.description: This register provides the status bits for the possible causes of an invalid mode interrupt.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: S_MRIG
bitfields.description: Mode Request Ignored status — This bit is set whenever a new mode is requested while a transition to the SAFE mode is in progress. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit. This bit is also set when a transition to STANDBY0/STOP0 mode is requested while a wakeup event is active.

sub_bitfields.description: Mode transition requested is not illegal

bitfields.name: S_MTI
bitfields.description: Mode Transition Illegal status — This bit is set whenever a new mode is requested while some other non- SAFE mode transition process is active (S_MTRANS is ‘1’). Please refer to Mode Transition Interrupts for the exceptions to this behavior. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: Mode transition requested is not illegal

bitfields.name: S_MRI
bitfields.description: Mode Request Illegal status — This bit is set whenever the target mode requested is not a valid mode with respect to current mode. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: Target mode requested is not illegal with respect to current mode
Target mode requested is illegal with respect to current mode

bitfields.name: S_DMA
bitfields.description: Disabled Mode Access status — This bit is set whenever the target mode requested is one of those disabled modes determined by ME_ME register. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: Target mode requested is not a disabled mode
Target mode requested is a disabled mode

bitfields.name: S_NMA
bitfields.description: Non-existing Mode Access status — This bit is set whenever the target mode requested is one of those non existing modes determined by ME_ME register. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: Target mode requested is an existing mode
Target mode requested is a non-existing mode

bitfields.name: S_SEA
bitfields.description: SAFE Event Active status — This bit is set whenever the chip is in SAFE mode, SAFE event bit is pending and a new mode requested other than RESET/SAFE modes. It is cleared by writing a ‘1’ to this bit.

sub_bitfields.description: No new mode requested other than RESET/SAFE while SAFE event is pending
New mode requested other than RESET/SAFE while SAFE event is pending

registers.description: This register provides the status of different factors which influence mode transitions. It is used to give an indication of why a mode transition indicated by ME_GS.S_MTRANS may be taking longer than expected.

bitfields.name: PREVIOUS_MODE
bitfields.description: Previous chip mode — These bits show the mode in which the chip was prior to the latest change to the current mode. NOTE: Mode codes “1001”, “1011”, “1100”, “1110”, and “1111” are reserved and should never appear.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: MPH_BUSY
bitfields.description: MC_ME/MC_PCU Handshake Busy indicator — This bit is set if the MC_ME has requested a mode change from the MC_PCU and the MC_PCU has not yet completed its power-up/down sequencing. It is cleared when the MC_PCU has power-up/down sequencing.

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: PMC_PROG
bitfields.description: MC_PCU Mode Change in Progress indicator — This bit is set if the MC_PCU is in the process of powering up or down power domains. It is cleared when all power-up/down processes have completed.

sub_bitfields.description: Power-up/down transition is not in progress

bitfields.name: DBG_MODE
bitfields.description: Debug mode indicator — This bit is set while the chip is in debug mode.

sub_bitfields.description: The chip is not in debug mode
The chip is in debug mode

bitfields.name: CCKL_PROG
bitfields.description: Core Clock Enable/Disable in Progress — This bit is set while any core’s clock is in the process of being enabled or disabled.

sub_bitfields.description: No core clock is being enabled or disabled
A core clock is being enabled or disabled

bitfields.name: PCS_PROG
bitfields.description: Progressive System Clock Switching in Progress — This bit is set while the progressive system clock switching process is in progress. The PCS_PROG bit is set when the • PCS is in progress or • Peripheral clock switching is ongoing or • Core clock switching is ongoing or • Power sequence process is ongoing (provided the target mode is not STANDBY)

bitfields.name: SMR
bitfields.description: SAFE mode request from MC_RGM is active indicator — This bit is set if a hardware SAFE mode request has been triggered. It is cleared when the hardware SAFE mode request has been cleared.

sub_bitfields.description: A SAFE mode request is not active
A SAFE mode request is active

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: Clock Disable Process Pending status for Peripherals 0…255 This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

sub_bitfields.description: No peripheral clock disabling is pending
Clock disabling is pending for at least one peripheral

bitfields.name: VREG_CSRC_SC
bitfields.description: Main VREG dependent Clock Source State Change during mode transition indicator — This bit is set when a clock source which depends on the main voltage regulator to be powered-up is requested to change its power up/down state. It is cleared when the clock source has completed its state change.

sub_bitfields.description: No state change is taking place
A state change is taking place

bitfields.name: CSRC_CSRC_SC
bitfields.description: (Other) Clock Source dependent Clock Source State Change during mode transition indicator — This bit is set when a clock source which depends on another clock source to be powered-up is requested to change its power up/down state. It is cleared when the clock source has completed its state change.

sub_bitfields.description: No state change is taking place
A state change is taking place

bitfields.name: IRC_SC
bitfields.description: IRC State Change during mode transition indicator — This bit is set when the 16 MHz internal RC oscillator is requested to change its power up/down state. It is cleared when the 16 MHz internal RC oscillator has completed its state change.

sub_bitfields.description: No state change is taking place
A state change is taking place

bitfields.name: SCSRC_SC
bitfields.description: Secondary Clock Sources State Change during mode transition indicator — This bit is set when a secondary clock source is requested to change its power up/down state. It is cleared when all secondary system clock sources have completed their state changes. (A ’secondary clock source’ is a clock source other than IRC.)

sub_bitfields.description: No state change is taking place
A state change is taking place

bitfields.name: SYSCLK_SW
bitfields.description: System Clock Switching pending status —

sub_bitfields.description: No system clock source switching is pending
A system clock source switching is pending

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: FLASH_SC
bitfields.description: FLASH State Change during mode transition indicator — This bit is set when the FLASH is requested to change its power up/down state. It is cleared when the DFLASH has completed its state change.

sub_bitfields.description: No state change is taking place
A state change is taking place

bitfields.name: Reserved
bitfields.description: This field is reserved. This read-only field is reserved and always has the value 0.

bitfields.name: CDP_PRPH_96_
bitfields.description: 127 Clock Disable Process Pending status for Peripherals 96…127 — This bit is set when any peripheral appearing in ME_PS3 has been requested to have its clock disabled. It is cleared when all these peripherals which have been requested to have their clocks disabled have entered the state in which their clocks may be disabled. Peripheral n corresponds to the ME_PCTLn register. Please refer to memeory map table for the ME_PCTLn locations actually occupied, which in turn indicates which peripherals are reported in the ME_DMTS register.

sub_bitfields.description: No peripheral clock disabling is pending
Clock disabling is pending for at least one peripheral

registers.description: This register controls whether the Z4A is disabled or running during run modes. Please refer to memory map table for information on which ME_CCTL1 locations are actually occupied. The unoccupied locations contain a read-only half-word value of 0x0000. The run mode bits (SAFE, DRUN, and RUNx) of the ME_CCTL1 register are pre-loaded with the value provided by the device configuration just before reset exist. The value of the DRUN bit just before entering STANDBY0 mode is the value of all the run mode bits (SAFE, DRUN, and RUNx) on STANDBY0 exit. The values of the low- power mode bits (STOP0, and STANDBY0) revert to their reset values on STANDBY0 exit. The low-power mode bits (STOP0, and STANDBY0) of the ME_CCTL1 register are reset with the default value shown and are not pre-loaded with another value.

registers.description: This register contain the boot address of each Z4A and a bit for controlling whether the Z4A core is to be reset on the next mode change that has the core configured to be running in the target mode. This register can be written only as words and cannot be written after a mode change request has been made until the mode transition has completed (i.e., while the S_MTRANS bit of the ME_GS register = ‘1’). A write access to any of this register during this time will result in the ICONF_CC flag in the ME_IS register being asserted. ME_CADDR1 is pre-loaded with the value provided by the device configuration just before reset exit in order to ensure that Z4A boots from the correct address after any chip reset if the DRUN bit in the ME_CCTL1 register has a default value of ‘1’. The value of the ADDR field just before entering STANDBY0 mode is the value of the ADDR field on STANDBY0 exit.

bitfields.name: ADDR
bitfields.description: Core Address — This field is used by Z4A cores as the boot address (32-bit word aligned) when Z4A next exits reset.

bitfields.name: RMC
bitfields.description: Reset on Mode Change The Z4A will be reset on the next mode change that has the core configured to be running in the target mode. 0 Z4A will not be reset on the next mode change 1 Z4A will be reset on the next mode change that has the core configured to be running in the target mode. This field is automatically cleared when the core reset triggered by the RMC is executed.

registers.description: This register contain the boot address of Z2 core and a bit for controlling whether the corresponding core is to be reset on the next mode change that has the Z2 core configured to be running in the target mode. This register can be written only as words and cannot be written after a mode change request has been made until the mode transition has completed (i.e., while the S_MTRANS bit of the ME_GS register = ‘1’). A write access to this register during this time will result in the ICONF_CC flag in the ME_IS register being asserted. ME_CADDR3 is pre-loaded with the value provided by the device configuration just before reset exit in order to ensure that Z2 core boots from the correct address after any chip reset if the DRUN bit in the ME_CCTL3 register has a default value of ‘1’. The value of the ADDR field just before entering STANDBY0 mode is the value of the ADDR field on STANDBY0 exit.

bitfields.name: LPU_STOP_ACK_BYPASS
bitfields.description: Bypass STOP acknowledge handshake with LPU domain modules (which are present in LPU_MDIS register), during LPU_STOP and LPU_SLEEP. NOTE: Modules should be IDLE before entering LPU_STOP/SLEEP, that is, no outstanding transactions or interrupts should be pending. Bypassing STOP ACK will enable entry in LPU_STOP/SLEEP irrespective of interrupt generated during the mode transition and then the same interrupt will cause mode exit. If STOP Handshake is not bypassed, mode transition may hang as modules will not acknowledge stop due to outstanding interrupt during the mode transition.

bitfields.name: ENET_RX_BS
